stages.title: Arrival & initial processing
stages.body: People brought to the UK enter initial processing. Officials collect and verify identity and other details, with immediate healthcare needs addressed. Initial processing is distinct from the later decision on an asylum claim.

stages.title: Register an asylum claim
stages.body: A person seeking protection tells an immigration officer. Screening records identity, photographs and fingerprints, the reason for claiming, and relevant medical information. An interpreter can be requested. Registration does not itself grant refugee status.

stages.title: Decide where the claim is considered
stages.body: The Home Office considers whether to examine the claim in the UK. A safe-third-country connection may trigger an inadmissibility process. Transfer depends on applicable arrangements and the individual case; arrival from France does not mean every person is automatically returned.

stages.title: While the case is pending
stages.body: Eligible people who cannot support themselves may receive accommodation and financial support. Reporting requirements can apply. Some people may be detained; others are not. Children and people with particular vulnerabilities require different consideration.

stages.title: Evidence & asylum interview
stages.body: Where the claim is examined, the applicant explains why they fear return and supplies supporting evidence. A substantive interview explores the protection claim in more detail than screening. Interpretation is available where needed.

stages.title: Decision on protection
stages.body: A successful claim can lead to refugee status or humanitarian protection; other permission is possible. The length and conditions of permission depend on the applicable rules and claim date. Recognition is not automatic citizenship or permanent settlement.

stages.title: Appeal or departure
stages.body: A refusal may carry a right of appeal. If there is no remaining permission or legal basis to stay after the relevant process, departure may be voluntary or enforced. A refusal, an appeal outcome and an actual return are separate events.
